subject: Urgent: Migration pressure from Asterix — benchmark request and proposed save path
messages:
From: Leah Powers <leah@asterix.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@asterix.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Exploring Redwood — benchmarking request + procurement timeline

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the intro from Tom. We're at the tail end of a platform evaluation and BlueWave is currently the front-runner — their pricing and integration velocity are attractive. That said, we've been impressed with Redwood's latency claims and caching strategy and want to see objective numbers before making a final decision.

Can you run a side-by-side performance benchmark against our production-like workload? Key asks:
- 95th percentile gen latency for a 512-token context at baseline traffic (30 TPS) and peak (120 TPS)
- Token-level cost estimate for sustained monthly usage (~1.2B tokens)
- KV/prefix caching behavior for repeated prompts (we'll share a sample set)

Procurement timeline: we need a vendor selection decision by 2027-07-01 to make Q3 migration plans. Procurement will want evidence (run logs, configs) and proposed term/credits if we switch. I attached a short requirements sheet (ast-benchmark-requirements.xlsx).

Would appreciate a quick confirmation and a proposed cadence for the benchmark (we'd like results within 48–72 hours if possible).

Best,
Leah
Leah Powers
Head of ML Engineering, Asterix AI

---
Attachments:
ast-benchmark-requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12KB)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Leah Powers <leah@asterix.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 17:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring Redwood — benchmarking request + procurement timeline

Hi Leah — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. Olga here (Enterprise SDR for Midwest / Strategic Accounts).

We can run a focused, production-alike proof-of-performance. Proposed immediate plan:
1) Redwood will run two side-by-side runs using your sample prompts: a standard open-model stack and a quantized variant we recommend for cost parity.
2) We'll measure 95th/99th latency percentiles at the two TPS targets and produce token-cost estimates with realistic batching and KV caching enabled.
3) Deliverables: raw run logs (CSV), short run summary (PDF), and an exec one-pager you can share with procurement.

Can you:
- Share the sample payload set (we saw the requirements sheet; a small sample payload file will speed things)
- Confirm a technical contact for SSH/ingest if needed (we can accept S3 or secure link)

Looping in Ben (bench lead) and Marissa (customer success) to coordinate. Karthik will cover pricing and contract levers after we have numbers.

Options for a save path if numbers land in our favor: short-term committed capacity with a ramping discount, migration support hours, and a one-time credit for migration risk. We'll sketch that once we see the results.

I can schedule a 30-min call for Monday to align on run specifics — does 10:00am PT work for your team?

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov | Senior Accounts, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments:
bench-config.txt (text, 3KB); redwood-save-plan-v2.pdf (proposal stubs, 45KB)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: Asterix ask — quick bench plan and negotiation levers

Team — summary from Leah at Asterix (cc'd Tom): they want a fast, side-by-side performance/cost readout; procurement expects a vendor decision by 2027-07-01. This is higher-risk because BlueWave is incumbent and moving is painful for them.

Key technical constraints (from requirements sheet):
- 512-token average inference length, repeat prompt patterns for caching tests
- 30 TPS steady / 120 TPS peak for 10-minute windows
- Expectation: provide run logs + cost calc for sustained 1.2B tokens/month

Proposed bench plan (short):
- Run A: Redwood recommended model (FP16 / quant-opt) with default batching and prefix cache enabled
- Run B: Redwood minimal-cost config (quantized) to show delta in $/M tokens
- Inject synthetic burst to simulate 120 TPS for 10 minutes, with sequence length distribution attached

Deliverables we own: CSV run logs, pie of latency distribution, cost delta table, and an ops migration playbook snapshot for the exec one-pager.

Negotiation levers to prepare (Karthik):
- 6-month committed capacity at 10% below list with migration credit ($Xk)
- Canary rollback window + free migration assistance (50 hours Saas support)
- SLA exceptions for throughput during first 30 days

Ben — please run an initial pass tonight (I know tight) and flag any infra blockers. Marissa — be ready to join the exec call if numbers look promising. I can own deal communications with Leah/procurement.

Thanks — O.

---
Attachments:
benchmark-run-plan.md (internal run checklist)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Asterix ask — quick bench plan and negotiation levers

Quick lab update — ran the two side-by-side passes against the sample payload Leah shared. Summary below (high level):

- Run A (recommended): 95p latency = 210ms at 30 TPS; 95p latency = 360ms at 120 TPS (10-min burst). Avg tokens/sec throughput aligns with their expected distribution.
- Run B (cost-optimized quant): 95p latency = 260ms at 30 TPS; 95p = 470ms at peak. Cost delta: ~23% lower token cost vs Run A; vs BlueWave published numbers, Redwood shows ~12% lower token cost with comparable 95p at baseline.

Artifacts: attached CSV with raw run logs and a short results sheet. Notes: prefix caching reduced repeated prompt latency by ~35% in both runs — that'll be a strong ops differentiator.

Recommendation for save path (two-tier):
1) Term offer: 6-month committed capacity (commit to 300M tokens/month) with a 12% discount on usage + $40k migration credit and 40 hours of hands-on migration support.
2) Contingency: 30-day rollback clause and an SLA-backed latency target (95p under 400ms on sustained 30 TPS).

Karthik — rough cost delta and phrasing below you can adapt for commercial: list price equivalence, effective blended $/1M tokens, and one-time credit carve-out.

If we want to move fast I can package the run logs + an exec one-pager for procurement by EOD Monday.

Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0177

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Leah Powers <leah@asterix.ai>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@asterix.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, procurement@asterix.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exploring Redwood — benchmark results and proposed commercial path

Hi Leah / Tom — thanks for the quick turnaround on the sample payload and for being clear on timeline. We completed the side-by-side runs and attached the full logs and an executive summary. Short summary up front:

- Performance: Redwood meets your 95th percentile targets under baseline traffic and remains within acceptable latency headroom during the 120 TPS burst when caching is leveraged.
- Cost: Our cost-optimized config shows ~23% lower token cost (per Ben's run). Against BlueWave public numbers we appear ~12% more economical at baseline with comparable latency.

Proposed path to de-risk migration (what we suggest you take to procurement):
1) 6-month committed pilot: 300M tokens/month at a 12% discount + one-time migration credit of $40,000 and 40 hours dedicated migration support.
2) SLA: 95p latency target of <= 400ms for steady-state 30 TPS; monitoring/alerting will be accessible via Redwood Console during trial.
3) Rollback: 30-day canary with automated fallback to incumbent (we'll help script the fallback).

Deliverables we've attached/linked: run logs CSV, an exec one-pager (redwood-save-plan-v2.pdf), and a short ops playbook. Drive link with full artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-asterix-bench-results.

Next steps — proposed timeline:
- Tue 2027-06-22: 30-min call (exec + procurement) to review run artifacts and confirm terms
- Wed 2027-06-23: Procurement sends redlines / preferred legal template
- By 2027-07-01: vendor decision

Would you be available Tue 10:00am PT? If procurement prefers we can also provide a short table with cost-by-tier and a DocuSign-ready term sheet: https://www.docusign.com/link/agreements/AST-EXT-2027

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Olga
Olga Petrov | Senior Accounts, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
